source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Reversals Often End at Signal Bars from Prior Failed Reversals

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: BullReversalBarAtNewLow
candidates.quote: if there is a bear trend and there have been several bull entries that failed as the market continued to sell off, each of these entry prices and the highs of every signal bar will be targets
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a bull reversal signal bar attempt within a bear leg -- the bar makes a new N-bar low intraday but closes in the upper fraction of its own range.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] <= lowest(low, lookback)[1] && (close[0] - low[0]) >= reversalFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the signal bar's high

complexity.reason: a lowest-low window plus single-bar body arithmetic

notes: Brooks does not define 'signal bar' numerically here; this reading follows the reversal-bar convention used elsewhere in the trilogy.

candidates.name: FailedReversalAttempt
candidates.quote: there have been several bull entries that failed as the market continued to sell off
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a BullReversalBarAtNewLow whose stop entry triggered but the trend resumed -- price made a new low below the signal bar's low within failureWindow bars without first trading minMoveTicks above the entry trigger.
candidates.pseudocode: triggered = high[sb] reached within failureWindow bars of sb; failed = exists i in (sb, sb+failureWindow]: low[i] < low[sb] && high[i0..i] never reached high[sb] + minMoveTicks * tickSize for any i0 <= i
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (post-hoc classification of a failed stop entry)

complexity.reason: needs to remember a signal bar's trigger and scan forward to decide success vs failure before recording the level

notes: Brooks: the directional probability of an equidistant 10-tick move favors the trend by about 60 percent at the start of a leg -- read here as the minMoveTicks proxy for 'the reversal did not get far enough to count as a success.'

candidates.name: FailedReversalSignalBarExtremeAsTarget
candidates.quote: The market will often rally all the way to the highest signal bar's high before having a significant pullback.
candidates.description: Once a genuine reversal begins, the target/magnet is the highest high among all FailedReversalAttempt (bull) signal bars recorded during the prior bear leg; exit or expect resistance there.
candidates.pseudocode: target = max(signalBarHigh over all FailedReversalAttempt bars recorded since the leg began); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the highest failed-reversal signal bar's extreme

complexity.reason: must persist a running set of failed-attempt levels across an entire trend leg and take their extreme

notes: Brooks: traders who scaled into the losing counter-trend entries often exit breakeven on their worst (highest) entry, which is why that level in particular is the magnet.

candidates.name: DoubleTopAtFailedReversalLevel
candidates.quote: The rally often forms a double top with one of those earlier entry bars and then turns down, at least briefly, as the trading range evolves.
candidates.description: Filter/trigger: once price reaches the FailedReversalSignalBarExtremeAsTarget level and prints a bear reversal bar there, treat it as a probable double top and a valid countertrend short setup.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize && (high[0] - close[0]) >= reversalFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop below the reversal bar's low

complexity.reason: depends on the persisted failed-reversal target plus a reversal-bar test

notes: Overlaps with the double top / double bottom pattern formalized in Chapter 12 (double_top_bear_flags); the dedup pass should merge the two.

candidates.name: ReversalOnlyAtKeyTechnicalConfluence
candidates.quote: it is important to watch for these patterns when the market is at key technical levels, like at measured move targets, trend lines, and even higher time frame moving averages and trend lines
candidates.description: Filter: only treat a reversal pattern as high-probability when it forms at a remembered magnet level (measured-move target, trend line, higher-time-frame moving average or trend line), not in the open middle of a move.

complexity.reason: 'nearestMagnetLevel' is a design decision -- which of the many magnet families (measured move, trend line, higher-timeframe MA) is on offer is not specified

notes: Generalizes R08-14/R08-15's measured-move-specific gating to any magnet family; see Chapter 10 for the fuller magnet list.

rejected.quote: the directional probability of an equidistant move is at least 60 percent
rejected.reason: narrative statistical framing with no bar-computable threshold of its own; used only as informal motivation, not a decidable condition (the 60 percent figure is folded into R09-02's minMoveTicks proxy instead)

rejected.quote: it might simply be one of the many secret handshakes that all great traders know
rejected.reason: pure discretion / trader psychology speculation, no bar-level test

rejected.quote: Some firms will write programs based on one or more technical support levels, and other firms will use others.
rejected.reason: refers to other firms' unknown proprietary logic, not decidable from this engine's bars

chapter_summary: Short chapter arguing that failed reversal attempts leave behind signal-bar extremes that become magnets for the next successful reversal in that direction, often producing a double top/bottom when finally tested. It yields a chain of primitives (reversal signal bar, failed attempt, the persisted extreme-as-target) plus two context filters (double top at that level, reversal patterns are more reliable at any key technical confluence). The probability narrative in the middle of the chapter is descriptive color, not a separate rule.
